sections.overview: This western North American hawkmoth occurs from Oregon and California into the Southwest and northern Baja California.
sections.identification: Its gray forewings are darker in Oregon and central California, paler in much of the juniper belt.
sections.habitat: It inhabits desert and pinyon-juniper woodland, including dry forests with western juniper.
sections.diet: Caterpillars feed on junipers; adults take nectar from flowers including western chokecherry and California buckeye.
sections.behavior: Adults are nocturnal and fly in midsummer; the species is reported in one annual brood from late spring through summer.
sections.reproduction: The full-grown caterpillar pupates in an underground burrow and overwinters there.
sections.ecology: The caterpillar stage is associated with Cupressaceae, especially Juniperus and Calocedrus.
sections.conservation: Its reported global NatureServe rank is G4, Apparently Secure.
